runs.name: Fastenal Company
runs.entry: Price **$51.55** (2026-10-12, live quote from `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged) x **1,147,497,573 shares** (one class; 10-Q cover as of 2026-07-10, 0000815556-26-000041; checked against 1,147,494,415 issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30, no treasury stock, the 3,158 difference option exercises; the two-for-one split effective 2025-05-21 in every count) = cap **$59,153M**; net cash $84.7M at 2026-06-30, all-equity value $59,068M; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y, 2026-10-09). Primary document the FY2025 10-K (0000815556-26-000009), with the 10-Q of 2026-07-16, the DEF 14A of 2026-02-25 (0000815556-26-000017), the FY2016 and FY2020 to FY2023 10-Ks and the 8-Ks of 2025 and 2026 (interim CFO, split, auditor change KPMG to PwC, new CFO Max H. Tunnicliff, CEO transition Daniel L. Florness to Jeffery M. Watts on 2026-07-16, credit agreement of 2026-06-18); FY2025 operating cash $1,295.9M cross-checked to the filed cash-flow statement and total assets $5,052.9M to the filed balance sheet; 2007 to 2015 from XBRL, flagged as transcription. A distributor of industrial and construction supplies, about 96% made by others, through 1,595 branches, onsite locations, vending devices and bins in the customer's plant. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs (listed in Step 0 of the run). **Q1 IN** (a distributor whose ten-year economics can be foreseen from its own ten-year customer-site table and fifteen years of filings). **Q2 IN**: a low-cost, high-service delivery castle, stock placed inside the customer's plant (FMI 44.7% of 2025 sales, 74% under contract); operating margin 20% to 21.5% every year 2011 to 2025 and 15.3% in 2009 when sales fell 17.5%; highest of the three rivals every year 2017 to 2025 (Grainger 8.6% to 15.6%, MSC Industrial 13.1% falling to 8.0%, Applied Industrial 2.7% to 11.1%). **Q3 weighs for** (pre-tax return on capital employed 36% in 2016 to 44% in 2025, about 54% pre-tax on the capital added; about 31 cents of working capital per added sales dollar). **Q4 IN, weighs for** (ten balance sheets read: equity built from retained earnings, goodwill immaterial, receivables 12.6% to 15.2% of sales, inventory 25% to 21%, debt peak $555M in 2022 and $125M at end 2025; every real cost charged, no adjusted figure). **Q5 integrity IN, ability weighs for** (no restatement, no related-person transactions, misses reported plainly, internal successor named); recorded, not judged: the CFO resigned April 2025 with no stated reason, and KPMG, auditor for 38 years, was replaced by PwC after FY2024 with no disagreements reported. **Q6 weighs for, two marks against** (payout about 80%, retention passes, no stock deals; against: a bonus formula that pays again for recovering lost ground, and 1,075,000 shares bought in the first half of 2026 at $46.33, above the top of the range, under a programme with no stated price limit). **Q7 OUT**: owner cash 2021 to 2025 averages $932.1M ($937.1M before net interest), about $0.81 a share; owner growth 14.44% a year cut to the 8.07% sales rate by specific (f); value range **$14.66 to $27.75** a share all-equity ($14.51 to $27.54 equity-only; full-cycle base $13.95 to $26.42), literal window 2021 to 2025; the growth case returns 3.18% at the price and the uncut 14.44% case 5.06%, both below the 5.60% Treasury; fair price **$11.29** all-equity (central), $11.16 equity-only. Q8 to Q12 not reached; facts after the stop recorded (cash yield 1.59%; $835M revolver to 2031, leverage covenant step-up to 3.50 after a qualified acquisition written in June 2026). Strongest evidence against, set down by the analyst: gross margin about 50% (2015, 2016) to 45.0% (2025) and expected by the company to keep falling; unnamed online and non-traditional rivals; the FMI advantage that by the company's own risk factor "could be eliminated"; sourcing heavily concentrated in Asia. Competitors: the 10-K names none; the analyst took Grainger, MSC Industrial and Applied Industrial from the proxy's compensation peer group, confessed as a CONVENTION of the run, figures from XBRL. Contamination declared by the analyst: a listing of `Test Runs/` filtered for the name (nothing returned), the session's git status and commit subjects, the memory index; nothing used. Commits 60441178 to 2e20bc02, write-early kept (a commit after each question). Citations: the analyst's check 92 ids, 66 fragments, 0 problems; the dispatcher's adjacency script (`dispatcher_check.py`) 92 ids present, 52 adjacent fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold. check_framework PASS. Analyst's gaps for the operator: (1) specific (e)'s aberrational first or last year is unclear when owner cash swings on working capital; (2) two range specifics conflict: one forbids charging all spending and also capping growth, the other then cuts the growth rate; (3) the brief's competitor rule assumes the 10-K names rivals; (4) the framework does not say whether growth inside the ten years is nominal or real; (5) Q6's retention test needs historical prices, which operator rule 5 confines aggregators from supplying. Not obtained: scuttlebutt from rivals, customers or former staff; the rivals' and 2007 to 2015 figures read from filed statements rather than XBRL.
runs.narr: Q7 OUT on price: a castle of cheap, frequent, high-service delivery with stock inside the customer's plant, operating margin 20% to 21.5% every year 2011 to 2025 and highest of Grainger, MSC and Applied Industrial every year 2017 to 2025, equity built from retained earnings; but at $51.55 the value range is $14.66 to $27.75 all-equity and the growth case returns 3.18% against a 5.60% Treasury. Fair $11.29 all-equity ($11.16 equity-only), armed. Against: gross margin down five points in ten years and guided lower, the FMI advantage that "could be eliminated", 2026 buybacks at $46.33 above the range, CFO and auditor changes of 2025 recorded. The analyst asks how specific (e) treats a working-capital swing and how the growth cap meets the all-spending rule.
runs.fair_label: FAST at/below $11.29: the fair price on the all-equity basis of the blind v5 purchase run of 2026-10-12 (Test Runs/2026-10-12 Run - FAST Fastenal.md; OUT at Q7 at $51.55; $11.16 equity-only; literal FY2021-FY2025 window, growth cut to the 8.07% sales rate). A prompt to re-run Q7, never a verdict.
